The falsifier was NOT triggered; the fix is not falsified by this test.
contradicted: Two things: (1) The mission's own cited live evidence -- POST buildable-envelope {lat,lng} returning HTTP 504 at 10.2s for the Travis point -- did not reproduce in four separate live re-checks I ran before touching any code (1.4-1.6s, 200 OK, every time), nor in three more after the LDT fix deployed. I traced the full code path anyway (documented in CP1) and found every query on it already indexed/tile-partitioned/capped, unlike the actual pre-fix radius-search hang -- consistent with the mission's OWN F11 finding that this class of hang is 'intermittent, unmeasured.' I shipped the bounded-timeout-plus-refusal hardening the mission asked for regardless, since a fix that can't be proven wrong by a non-reproducing case is still a legitimate defensive improvement, but I did not claim to have reproduced or fixed a live incident I could not observe. (2) The implementing sub-agent's own LDT test (for the timeout path) hung real CI past Vitest's 20s default timeout because it mixed vi.useFakeTimers() with supertest's real HTTP round-trip -- a genuine regression in the sub-agent's first commit that its own reported 'clean typecheck' did not catch (since it never actually executed). Caught by real GitHub Actions CI (not by me proactively, though I had already flagged the untested state as a risk in CP2 before push), root-caused, and fixed in a follow-up commit; the second CI run passed clean, including that exact test, for real.
leaveBehind: Split-situs situs/city-separation shape: only checked Travis (48453) per this mission's scope. Did NOT check whether any other Central Texas county shares the same split-situs shape -- 'not checked', not 'checked and found only Travis'. This is the trigger named in OPS-23 section 5 and section 11 for the deferred per-county situs JOIN; whoever picks that up next should run the same check across 48021/48055/48209/48309/48491 before assuming Travis is unique.

legacy-design-tools' bounded timeout (POINT_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT_MS, 8s) is a client-side race, not query cancellation -- it stops the bare-504 symptom within a controlled window but does not relieve any underlying DB pool contention if that is the real root cause; the orphaned query (if the hang recurs) keeps running server-side. If P-160's probe instrument (not yet built) measures this hang recurring on three consecutive runs per OPS-23 section 11's own stated trigger, the next fix needs to go deeper (a DB-level statement_timeout or connection-pool investigation), which is explicitly larger than this mission's size cap.
